This haunting footage was captured moments before the fatal tiger mauling in Yorkshire. Footage has emerged appearing to show a man in his 20s approaching a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park shortly before he was killed inside the enclosure on Saturday, October 10. The man can be seen filming himself near five-year-old Siberian tiger Altai as horrified visitors shout ‘Oh my God’ from the viewing platform above. Onlookers reportedly tried to stop him climbing over the barrier and entering the enclosure. The park remains closed following the tragedy, while it has been confirmed that Altai will not be euthanised.

Grumpy Kallie is waiting for breakfast. 😊 Today, on International Tiger Day, we’re honored to introduce you to Kallie—a tiger whose survival is nothing short of a miracle. When Kallie was rescued by Lions Tigers & Bears, she had been abandoned and left to die. Her condition was so critical that she required extensive emergency medical care, multiple surgeries, and ultimately a life-saving leg amputation. Against all odds, Kallie never gave up. Today, Kallie is thriving on three legs, living the life she always deserved at Lions Tigers & Bears. She continues to receive specialized daily care from our dedicated team, and every step she takes is a reminder of what’s possible when compassion meets action. Your support made Kallie’s second chance possible. Thank you for standing with us as we rescue, rehabilitate, and provide lifelong sanctuary to animals who have nowhere else to turn. Happy International Tiger Day.

The man mauled to death by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park has been named and pictured as William Chapman. Footage posted to his Instagram appears to show him approaching the 200kg Siberian tiger shortly before the fatal attack. Witnesses say he climbed into the enclosure despite attempts to stop him. Emergency services attended, but Chapman died following the attack. The tiger will not be euthanised, and a health and safety investigation is underway.@Hannah Talks Politics
